title: Henri IV to Landgrave Maurice of Hesse-Kassel, ciphered passages printed in Rommel 1840

steps.what: Located cipher pages by digit density in the IA hOCR; fetched full-resolution page images.
Rommel's 1846 key (Allg. Zeitschrift f. Geschichte V, 402-403).
About 4,100 groups transcribed by eye with diacritics and glyphs.
Decode of the 3 Apr 1604 letter matches Rommel's 1846 clear text word for word.
All seven passages decoded and read; list misalignments in the print fixed from the texts.
Framing corrected: Rommel's key 'never applied' becomes 'no published application' after Lasry's note on overclaiming.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-letter transcriptions ct/*.txt, raw decodes letters/*_decode.txt and the hand readings letters/READINGS.md; key.py (Rommel 1846 key with the corrections).

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): p. 391 had been scored on its unspaced decode file (plain 0.0). The one ciphered phrase written into its clear sentence as letters/p391_reading.md: plain 1.0. Keeps read.

outcome.method_basis: The key is the one Rommel published in 1846 (Allgemeine Zeitschrift für Geschichte V, pp. 402-403) for the Henri IV-Maurice correspondence; the project transcribed the undeciphered figures from Rommel's 1840 edition and decoded them, correcting misplaced entries in the printed key.
outcome.notes: Open: nine groups p. 213, seven at top of p. 307, name 98_, a letter run on p. 311, stray garbled groups.

texts.label: 22 Nov 1602, Rommel p. 84
texts.summary: Henri IV asks the Landgrave for his promised advice on the coming Imperial diet, what to propose there for his allies, and whether to send his ambassador on to Saxony and Denmark.

texts.label: 12 Jan 1603, Rommel p. 99
texts.summary: With the Emperor absent from the diet, the King expects nothing important there, notably no election of a King of the Romans; he complains that the duc de Bouillon wrote nothing of the Administrator of Strasbourg's visit.

texts.label: 27 Dec 1604, Rommel pp. 211-214
texts.summary: The King explains why he has not sent an embassy to the German princes (the Protestants' disunity and their support for Bouillon), reports the United Provinces' resolve to fight on, and his trouble with Spanish intrigues and the comte d'Auvergne.

texts.label: 28 Apr 1605, Rommel p. 230
texts.summary: The passage Rommel regretted he could not decipher: the King's aid to the United Provinces and Geneva proves his care to maintain those of the reformed religion.

texts.label: Paris, 22 Dec 1605, Rommel pp. 269-272
texts.summary: After the Mérargues affair and the conspiracy in England the King urges the German princes to help the United Provinces with money and troops, promises to continue his own aid of two million livres, and asks what the Emperor intends at the diet.

texts.label: Fontainebleau, 20 May 1606, Rommel pp. 307-314
texts.summary: The King's programme against the Spanish-Habsburg design on the Imperial diet: the kings and princes jealous of Spain should concert in defence of 'la liberté germanique'; the King of England's neutrality, Spinola's coming campaign and the weakness of the States.

texts.label: 24 Jan 1609, Rommel p. 391
texts.summary: One line: the ministers of the Pope and the King of Spain will do all they can to reconcile Archduke Matthias with the Emperor.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1609 French): the sweep scored letters/p391_decode.txt, the unspaced decode in <> brackets with the clear text (plain 0.0, explicit 1.0). The 19 cipher groups are the subject of one clear sentence: 'les ministres du Pape et du Roi d'Espagne feront toutes sortes de debvoirs ... avec l'Empereur'. Written out as letters/p391_reading.md: plain 1.0, explicit 1.0 (one sentence). Too short for more than a check that the sentence holds; it does. Keeps read.

prior.where: Rommel 1846 printed the key and a clear text of the 3 Apr 1604 letter only; his 1840 'Passages déchiffrés' glossary guesses some phrases
